messages:
sara_ng: quick heads-up — I ran an Nsight Systems capture for the small-batch (batch=1) qkv-serving path during the perf test this morning. saw a recurring ~12–18ms memcpy spike on stream 2 that always precedes an INT8 kernel launch. looks like kernel selection flips right after the host->device copy and the copy seems to be blocking other kernels on stream 0/1

tyler_w: can you drop the qdrep? curious about the ordering (memcpy vs launch). does it look like memcpy is serialized to default stream?

sara_ng: uploaded qdrep and a perf csv: s3://redwood-traces/1719877777/trace.qdrep and s3://redwood-traces/1719877777/summary.csv 

jen_l: skimmed the waterfall — memcpy is on stream 2 but there are kernel launches on stream 0 that start earlier and then stall after the memcpy. CPU timeline shows a short ~2–3ms schedule gap right when the memcpy completes. could be host thread bounce.

michael_r: FYI perf-bot detected a regression on commit 4a9b7c — median p99 increased ~9ms for batch=1 on that model. commit message said "int8-election heuristic tweak". linking: https://git.internal/repo/commit/4a9b7c

perf-bot: regression-alert: model transformer-x, batch=1, baseline commit 3f2a -> current 4a9b7c, p99 19.8ms -> 28.9ms (+9.1ms). trace attached (see thread). :warning:

tyler_w: hypothesis: heuristic now prefers INT8 kernel variant but that variant triggers a different prefetch pattern — extra host->device memcpy for re-quant tables which happens on stream 2 and wins a lock on the copy engine, delaying subsequent compute kernels. also if CPU thread is preempted right at the memcpy->launch handoff we get a scheduling gap that serializes the stream work onto the copy engine.

sara_ng: reproduced locally with --repeat 200, attached a trimmed qdrep (50MB) and an nvprof snippet. command I used: ```nsys profile --output=run-1719877777 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./bench --model transformer-x --batch 1 --reps 200```

jen_l: nice. looking at NVTX ranges, there are two kernels labeled INT8_FWD and a small CAST_INT kernel that only shows up with the new path. CAST_INT is launched on stream 2 and has a hostmem copy right before it. timing: hostcopy 1.4ms, CAST_INT launch 0.2ms, then 3ms wait before the larger GEMM.

michael_r: that wait lines up with CPU scheduling gap seen in perf: sched_wakeup latency ~2.8ms for the worker thread that issues the GEMM launch. if the thread is preempted after the memcpy returns we lose the async handoff and kernels effectively serialize.

tyler_w: quick mitigation idea: change batcher to prefer same-kernel-path grouping for in-flight reqs — keep INT8-preferring requests together so we avoid flipping kernel variants mid-batch burst. second, try launching the CAST_INT and GEMM from the same CUDA stream or use cudaStreamWaitEvent placement so the copy doesn't block other streams.

sara_ng: tried forcing stream affinity (all launches to stream 0) for that path — tail improved ~6ms in local runs. but that increases contention for other high-priority requests.

jen_l: can we instead bump priority of compute streams so memcpy on low-priority stream doesn't stall compute? Also consider a small hostside yield: after the memcpy complete callback do a pthread_yield to reduce chance of preemption at the exact handoff point. odd but might help on noisy hosts.

michael_r: adding NVTX around the prefetch and cast path would help us quantify frequency of the flip in production traces. we should also instrument the kernel selector to emit a choice tag (FP16|INT8|INT8-cast) into the trace via nvtxPush.

perf-bot: experiment-suggestion: try experiment int8-cast-stream-affinity: group int8-cast and gemm on same stream vs separated streams; measure p99 for 10k inferences.

sara_ng: next steps I took: 1) added NVTX tags, 2) ran an affinity experiment (cast+gemm on same stream), 3) ran on a noisy host and a quiet host. results: same-stream = p99 21.2ms (noisy host) vs separated = 29.6ms. quiet host both are ~18–20ms. so host CPU preemption amplifies the issue.

tyler_w: sounds like two orthogonal fixes: short-term config change (same-stream affinity for that kernel combo) + longer-term fix (avoid extra hostcopy in int8 path by caching re-quant tables on device or multiplexing them across contexts).

jen_l: filed a bug: PERF-3221 — "int8 kernel path triggers hostmem copy that serializes copy-engine and is sensitive to CPU preemption" with traces attached. assigning to runtime/kernel-team.

michael_r: for the rollout: recommend canary the affinity fix only for batch=1 traffic and monitor p99 and CPU wakeups. include fallback to previous kernel selector if p99 regressed.

sara_ng: I can prepare a small patch to force same-stream for the cast->gemm segment and a config flag to control it. will measure on the lab rig and then canary.

tyler_w: thanks — please add the NVTX changes too so we keep collecting better telemetry. :+1:

jen_l: one more note — check whether our allocator pins the staging buffer as host-pinned memory. pinned vs pageable changes memcpy performance and whether it uses async engines. I saw both variations across traces.

sara_ng: good call — will include pinned vs pageable toggle in the next run. will post updated qdrep+summary when done.

michael_r: great thread. ended up being a subtle interaction of kernel selection, extra hostcopy, and CPU scheduling gaps. lesson: instrument selector and keep critical launch handoffs on the same stream.

perf-bot: tracking tags added: PERF-3221, experiment:int8-cast-stream-affinity, trace:1719877777
